topic: colibri, a pure-C engine that runs GLM-5.2 (744B MoE) in 25 GB of RAM

scenes.illustrates: The wordmark names colibri at frame 0 and the tagline states the whole thesis (a 744B model, 25 GB of RAM) as the hook, so the poster already carries the impossible pairing.
The received wisdom, sized large with the datacenter line in ember, is stated plainly so the video has a myth to break.
The 370 GB dormant on disk beside the 9.9 GB actually resident makes the sparsity a spatial fact, not a number in a sentence.

scenes.label: it wakes a few experts
scenes.illustrates: A field of expert-nodes sits dim while only a few flare and converge into a glowing core, so 'it wakes a few experts each token' becomes literally visible rather than claimed.

scenes.caption: the whole footprint
scenes.illustrates: The full memory footprint slams full-frame on a bright ember field, landing the impossible number right after we have seen why it is possible.
The engine itself, in plain mono, shows how little it takes: one C file, no BLAS, no Python, no GPU, no Docker.

scenes.subtitle: tiny engine, immense model.
scenes.illustrates: The pairing restated (744B model, 25 GB of RAM) rhymes with the open so the autoloop replays the thesis, and 'tiny engine, immense model' names the whole idea.
